To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the BiP-derived peptide, HLA-DR4-restricted, and RA patient–derived T cell stimulatory epitope (BiP-DR4-RA) was able to induce T cell responses in PBMCs from patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA).

the BiP epitope BiP(1–20) can stimulate the proliferation of CD4+ T cells from RA patients, that the BiP(1-20) epitope can stimulate the proliferation and differentiation of T cells from healthy donors, and that the BiP (1–20) peptide can induce regulatory T cell responses.

the HLA–DRB1*0401-restricted BiP-derived peptide, BiP 1-11 (QVPLLRVSRV), stimulates the proliferation and differentiation of autoreactive T cells, and the HLA– DRB1*0405-restricted BiP peptide, BiP (QVPLLRLVSRV) 2-12, inhibits autoreactive T cell proliferation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of BiP-derived peptides in RA pathogenesis.
the role of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) chaperone BiP in the development of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and the mechanisms by which BiP may contribute to the development of RA.
the identification of HLA–DRB1*0401-restricted BiP-derived peptides that can induce the expansion of autoreactive T cells in RA patients.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the data support the hypothesis that BiP-derived peptides are able to induce both inflammatory and regulatory T cells.
the data are consistent with the hypothesis that BiP is a self antigen in RA and that the presence of autoantibody to BiP in RA patients is associated with the presence of autoreactive T cells.
the role of BiP as a target antigen in RA is still unclear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we found a peptide that is presented by DR4 that can stimulate CD4+ T cells from RA patients.
BiP is not the culprit, but the victim.

BiP is an autoantigen that is recognized by CD4 T cells in the periphery of patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) and that the immunodominant BiP epitope recognized by these cells can be presented by HLA-DRB1*0401 and HLA-DR1*0404.
The main takeaway from our work is that
BiP peptides can be used to expand T cells in RA patients.
the immunodominant BiP epitopes that we identified were not associated with the induction of inflammatory T cells in PBMCs from RA patients.
BiP is a complex protein that contains multiple HLA–DR–restricted epitopes that are recognized by CD4+ T cells.
